item.title: European Commission warns Malta's budget risks breaching EU spending limits
item.description: The European Commission said Malta's draft budgetary plan is at risk of material non-compliance with the EU's maximum net expenditure growth limit, singling out energy tariff subsidies as a key factor. Net expenditure is projected to rise 10.2% in 2026, well above the 5.8% ceiling recommended by the EU Council, and by 6.3% in 2027. The Commission noted the fiscal cost of untargeted energy subsidies is set to climb from 0.9% of GDP in 2025 to around 1.8% in 2026, and called on Malta to act. The draft plan was submitted on 15 October, 11 days before Budget day.

item.title: Government to set up dedicated agency for Malta in Motion in 2027
item.description: Transport Minister Chris Bonett told Parliament that a dedicated agency would be established in 2027 to coordinate the Malta in Motion masterplan, which combines buses, ferries, walking, cycling, parking and a proposed rail service. He said the government is exploring larger car parks on town outskirts linked to circular bus routes, with Marsaskala flagged as a first test case, and that national parking and walking strategies are due in 2027. Bonett also said the bus network needs improvement and that more circular routes are planned for Rabat, Pembroke and the Three Cities.

item.title: 55 women murdered since 1970, 65% by current or former partners
item.description: The Malta Observatory on Femicide said at least 55 women have been killed in Malta since 1970, with 36 of the cases (65%) involving a current or former intimate partner. Twenty killings occurred during an ongoing abusive relationship and 16 in the context of an actual or planned separation. The Observatory issued its appeal ahead of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, recalling the recent murders of Charlotte Zammit, Miriam Azzopardi and Mary Grace Cassar.

item.title: Another mobile phone found in prison cell during night raid
item.description: A mobile phone was found in a prison cell on Tuesday evening, a month after three prisoners were similarly found in possession of phones. Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said the raid was carried out by prison officers and police as part of an investigation running several weeks. The three prisoners previously caught with phones include George Degiorgio and Robert Agius, convicted over the killing of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, and Damiano Torrisi; Agius and Torrisi were suspected of using phones to plot a murder. Bedingfield said possession of phones in prison is to be made a crime.

item.title: University academics to withhold exam marks over unpaid arrears
item.description: The University of Malta Academic Staff Association has told members not to publish examination or assignment results until arrears owed under their collective agreement are paid in full, saying no guarantee was given that the money would be paid with the January paycheque. The union declared an industrial dispute on 5 November after November's paycheque omitted arrears stemming from a May collective agreement, approved by 95% of members, that runs to 2029. Professors are estimated to be owed between €25,000 and €30,000, with lower bands due between €10,000 and €20,000.

item.title: Controversial Rahal Ġdid UCA development set to be refused
item.description: The Planning Authority is expected to refuse application PA/7261/26, which proposes replacing two townhouses on Triq l-Arkata near the 17th-century parish church of St Ubaldeska, a Grade 1 scheduled property. The proposal, lodged by G3 Estates Ltd, would build a complex with 12 underground parking spaces, two maisonettes, 20 apartments and a pool house. The authority received over 600 individual objections by the 20 November deadline, including one organised by the parish signed by 236 people, and the case officer has entered a negative recommendation in his report.

item.title: Man, 20, charged with raping 18-year-old on St Julian's rocky beach
item.description: A 20-year-old man was charged in court with raping an 18-year-old woman at the rocky beach in San Ġiljan, it emerged on Wednesday. The accused, Toby Jude Dixon Raphael, a Malta-born holder of a British passport who works in iGaming, was identified and arrested on Monday. The prosecution told the court this was the second such charge against him in the past 18 months and asked for his name to be published so other victims may come forward; the court ordered publication, and the defence asked for bail, which was opposed.

item.title: Swimmer airlifted to safety from Coral Lagoon at Mellieħa
item.description: A swimmer was airlifted to safety on Tuesday afternoon after she got into difficulty at the Coral Lagoon near l-Aħrax in Mellieħa and could not climb out. The Armed Forces of Malta said a helicopter hoisted her out of the area, with Civil Protection Department rescuers, an ambulance crew and Malta Red Cross first aiders also on scene. The Coral Lagoon is a natural collapsed sea cave connected to the open sea, popular for kayaking, snorkelling, paddleboarding and photography.

item.title: Malta Polo Club petitions government over Marsa grounds
item.description: Malta Polo Club has launched a petition calling on the government to return its historic grounds in Marsa, after the club was left without its main pitch and clubhouse following redevelopment works. Around 8,500 spectators watched the Cawnpore Cup on 21 June 2025 before the club handed over the grounds for redevelopment and packed up its clubhouse; the pitch has still not been returned and the clubhouse has since been demolished. The club is asking for the polo ground to be removed from the wider Marsa racecourse concession and a direct long-term emphyteutic lease granted instead.

item.title: Public Works objects to two Qormi rezoning applications over flood risk
item.description: The Public Works Department has objected to two separate Qormi applications seeking to rezone land for residential development, warning they could increase flood risks for neighbouring properties and undermine future flood mitigation. Both objections, dated 13 November, were signed by Mario Ellul, director of the PWD's Coastal and Stormwater Directorate. The first concerns a 4,297 sq m vacant site on Triq Amleto Spiteri proposed for five-storey residential blocks, while the second covers a smaller 360 sq m partly residential site near Triq l-Għoxrin ta' Jannar.
